chapter: Boston roadhouses and the Army band
title: Armistice, Brest delousing, Newport News and discharge
summary: He recalls the armistice shooting, six months waiting at Brest, a Newport News lecture and Chicken Richards's arrest, and discharge at Dix.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah, and anyway the war was over, there was more people killed on that November 11th than there
was during the war because they got out there and start firing the guns.
Yes, it was in 1918 and when we got ready to come home, we went to Brest, and now Brest is way up on a hill and we went to - delousedus and they give us summer underwear.
How did they delouse you, give you some kind of chemical.

No, they put you under a shower and the guys would throw that stuff all over and that's how I lost my hair, I think, because all that stuff got in my hair but anyway we got deloused and got cold up there so I went to the commissary and I asked them for some heavy underwear, so I got the underwear and put it on and they called inspection one day, they called inspection and here I am with this heavy underwear on and the officer says go on and take that off and get yourself some underwear.
And we stayed up there on Brest for six months before we could get a boat to come back to New York.

After the war was over and then we went into Newport News and I know we went down there -- in Virginia, we landed there and we went into camp there and the boss of the place he ordered us to go into the and hear a

lecture and one of our guys says we ain't going to have no lecture and he said we've been over there and serving in all that war and everything, you're going to lecture us and they put -- I says, let's go over there and don't have no argument because they'll put you in jail here and you won't get out because we're supposed to go back up to Dix --
No, he was Chicken Richards. Used to be up at Small's and he --
What did he do, dance or sing or what.

No, he was in F Company, and I was in with the band and so we all got in Newport News and he wanted to go -- don't go to no lecture, so they put him -- they arrested him for disobeying and I told him afterwards, I said, man, you got an hour or so, listen. You ain't got to pay any attention what it is.
So about six days later we went up to Dix and then we were deloused again and discharged. I come back to New York.
